subject: Dedicated commit sizing and discount path for Helio Medical
messages:
From: Sara Choe <sara.choe@heliomed.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: Matt Rivera <matt.rivera@heliomed.com>
Date: 2026-08-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Helio workload profile & ask for Dedicated sizing

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're close to deciding on a Dedicated route but need a concrete sizing + pricing proposal to present to procurement. Quick background below and I attached a sample of real traffic (helio_workload_sample.csv).

Summary:
- Primary workload: clinical summarization + extraction (mix of long inputs + structured output).
- Avg requests/day: ~20k (mostly during 9am-6pm PT), avg 350 req/min during business hours, peak observed 1,100 req/min for 10–15 minute bursts.
- Median input length: ~900 tokens; median output: ~300 tokens. We expect NLU-heavy instructions so KV cache hit for follow-ups is ~30%.
- Concurrent active users: ~75 (most produce short bursts), sustained concurrency target ~120 to cover spikes.
- Latency target: p95 end-to-end < 450ms for turnkey model calls.

Ask: can you size a Dedicated GPU pool (recommended GPU type + count), recommended reserved commit length (6 vs 12 mo) and pricing bands / discount ranges? Also confirm whether burst capacity or autoscale will cover the 1,100 req/min spikes and how credits vs overage are handled.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Choe
Head of AI Platform
Helio Medical

--- Attachment: helio_workload_sample.csv (CSV stub, 12k lines) ---

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Sara Choe <sara.choe@heliomed.com>
Cc: Connor OBrien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-18T13:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Helio workload profile & ask for Dedicated sizing

Sara,

Appreciate the workload extract — that helps a lot. I've run a quick sizing pass with Connor and Neha and put a conservative recommended config below. I attached an initial pricing memo (redwood_dedicated_pricing_v3.pdf) with three commit bands. High-level summary first, then sizing math + notes.

High-level recommendation (conservative):
- Pool: 8 x A100 80GB (or equivalent) dedicated GPU pool serving a primary model bundle (13B/33B-class quantized variants) + a warm fallback on a smaller 7B for low-latency traces.
- Expected steady throughput supported: ~350 req/min with p95 latency ~300–400ms (based on your median tokens + 30% KV cache).
- Peak handling: pool plus burst allowance for an additional ~800 req/min for short bursts (10–20 min) via our burst capacity allocator. For sustained loads above burst for >30min we recommend scaling to 12 x A100 or moving to the 12-mo commit tier.
- Recommended commit: 12-month reserved commit to secure the best pricing and capacity SLAs. 6-month is possible but discounts are ~8–12% smaller and capacity priority is lower.

Sizing notes / rough math (simplified):
- Median total tokens per request: ~1,200 (900 in + 300 out).
- Effective tokens served per minute at 350 req/min = 420k tokens/min.
- With continuous batching + KV cache we estimate a 3.5x efficiency multiplier; conservative GPU throughput per A100 at this profile gives us the 8-GPU recommendation.
- Concurrency: with 8 GPUs and smart routing we can keep p95 in your target for the steady-state concurrency ~120; short peaks covered by burst allocator.

Pricing & discount bands (see attached for line items):
- 6-mo commit: baseline monthly $XX,XXX; approximate discount vs on-demand: 18%
- 12-mo commit: baseline monthly $YY,YYY; approximate discount vs on-demand: 28%
- Enterprise add-on (SLA 99.9%, priority capacity): +10% to commit price or available as a separate premium SKU.

Open items / questions for your team:
1) Do you expect a higher KV cache hit rate for multi-turn sessions (we assumed 30%)?
2) Any hard requirement around model family (if you want to pin to 70B-class models we will need to size for H100s or a larger pool).
3) Procurement cadence: are you open to a 12-month commit with quarterly usage true-ups or do you need monthly?

Connor / Neha — I flagged this as a priority for a tight commercial path. Connor, can you draft a 12-mo commit figure with the 28% discount and an alternate 6-mo figure so we can share with Sara/procurement?

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Head of Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

--- Attachment: redwood_dedicated_pricing_v3.pdf (summary pricing memo) ---

From: Connor OBrien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Sara Choe <sara.choe@heliomed.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-19T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed 6-mo & 12-mo commit pricing (ballpark) for Helio

Sara, Laura — looping back with the ballpark commercial numbers Connor agreed to produce. These are meant for procurement review; final DocuSign-ready language will be produced once terms are agreed.

Option A — 6-month reserved commit
- Dedicated pool: 8 x A100 80GB
- Monthly commit: $54,000/mo (billed monthly)
- Discount: ~18% off on-demand equivalent
- Burst allowance: additional 800 req/min capacity for up to 20 cumulative hours/month (overage billed at on-demand rate)
- SLA: 99.5% availability (standard)

Option B — 12-month reserved commit (preferred)
- Dedicated pool: 8 x A100 80GB + 2x burst H100 warm slots (regional)
- Monthly commit: $44,000/mo (billed monthly)
- Discount: ~28% off on-demand equivalent
- Burst allowance: additional 1,200 req/min for up to 40 cumulative hours/month
- SLA: 99.9% availability, capacity priority for scheduled windows

Notes:
- We can include a quarterly true-up to move you between commit tiers if usage trends higher.
- Early termination: standard buyout (2 months of remaining commit) unless you convert to a lower-tier commit.

Next steps: if Helio is comfortable with Option B we will prepare a DocuSign with the scope of services and a data processing addendum (SOC2 evidence attached on request).

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

--- Attachment: qa_matrix_soc2_evidence.zip (stub) ---

From: Matt Rivera <matt.rivera@heliomed.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, Connor OBrien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Choe <sara.choe@heliomed.com>
Date: 2026-08-20T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed 6-mo & 12-mo commit pricing (ballpark) for Helio

Laura / Connor — appreciate the quick turn. Procurement reviewed Option B and had two asks: (1) can you nudge the 12-mo monthly price to $38k/mo (Helio has a hard budget line and needs a bigger discount); (2) can we get a guaranteed throughput SLA clause for scheduled business hours (9am–6pm PT) to cover p95 latency and capacity for the core 350 req/min steady state? If guaranteed throughput is not possible, can you provide a credit schedule for missed capacity SLOs?

Also, procurement prefers quarterly billing vs monthly. If you can do $38k/mo we can sign a 12-mo with quarterly billing and a standard DPA.

Thanks — Matt
Matt Rivera
Director of Procurement
Helio Medical

On attachments: we may request SOC2 artifacts if we proceed.

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Matt Rivera <matt.rivera@heliomed.com>, Sara Choe <sara.choe@heliomed.com>
Cc: Connor OBrien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-21T14:55:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed 6-mo & 12-mo commit pricing (ballpark) for Helio — counteroffer and SLO proposal

Matt/Sara — great, thanks for the clarity. We can accommodate a commercial path that hits Helio's budget with a few adjustments. Proposal below:

Counteroffer (12-mo commit, quarterly billing):
- Monthly commit: $38,000/mo (billed quarterly at $114,000/quarter)
- Dedicated pool: 8 x A100 80GB + 2 warm H100 slots for short high-compute fallbacks
- SLA & throughput SLO: guaranteed capacity to sustain 400 req/min steady-state during business hours (9am–6pm PT) with p95 latency target <= 450ms for the pinned model bundle. For capacity shortfalls we will provide credits: 5% monthly credit for each cumulative hour of degraded capacity (p95 > 450ms) up to 30% cap.
- Burst allowance: covered up to additional 1,000 req/min for 40 hours/month; overage billed at on-demand rate thereafter.
- SOC2/DPA: we will provide SOC2 evidence via secure link and include a standard DPA append in the DocuSign.
- Termination / true-up: quarterly true-up windows to adjust commit tier if usage materially exceeds the committed baseline for two consecutive quarters.

We view this as a balanced outcome — Helio gets the budgetary certainty you requested and explicit capacity SLOs; Redwood gets a 12-mo commitment so we can prioritize capacity and put the warm H100 slots in place. If Helio accepts, Connor will produce the final commercial paper + DocuSign link.

Action items for Helio: confirm the SOC2 artifact list and accept the SLO credit approach. Once confirmed we'll send the DocuSign in 24 hours.

Laura Bennett
Head of Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
